feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector leadership: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in director/consulting leadership; this strengthens credibility and seniority.  
- Good use of scale and scope indicators: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” etc.  
- Strong alignment between headline, competencies, projects, and experience; the positioning as a digital platform and communications systems leader is consistent.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across sections: “digital strategy,” “governance,” “workflows,” “editorial systems,” and “multimedia” appear many times. Consolidate skills/technical sections to avoid overlap.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities. Several bullets describe what you led or built, but fewer show measurable results, efficiency gains, audience growth, or business impact.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; maintain consistent punctuation in lists; “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, learning)” or “French (basic working proficiency).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and fewer broad capability lists.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years’ experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Add clearer outcome/value language, e.g. “for complex, mission-driven organizations” → “to improve discoverability, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement.”
- Reduce the long capability stack; keep 3–5 priority areas most relevant to recent roles: web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial systems, AI-enabled search/UX.
- Consider aligning with the subtitle by emphasizing leadership of digital platforms and communications systems rather than listing multimedia separately.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance models/content operations” and the long capability list overlap heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” is broad; recent experience supports “AI-enabled search and discovery” more specifically.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and with slightly tighter, more executive-level wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording for consistency: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations
- Clarify newer/high-value areas: AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations
- Refine sector language for impact: Public-sector advocacy communications instead of “Advocacy and public-sector communications”
- Consider a more concise final line: Multimedia production, studio and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled… experiences,” and “multimedia production” repeat language already used in the header.
- This section also overlaps with Topline Skills; keep competencies broad here and leave tools/platforms to later sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with Work Experience. Tightening phrasing, standardizing style, and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in and convert each item to a cleaner, parallel format: “Project name: action + platform/format + purpose/outcome.”
- Tighten wording and reduce stacked nouns, e.g., “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat.”
- Standardize style and punctuation across entries; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.
- Consider adding one concrete result, audience, or scale detail where available to strengthen impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and the advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in recent NACo roles.
- The footer should complement, not restate, Work Experience; consider framing these as selected examples of current/recent work only.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads like a capability list and overlaps heavily with earlier NACo entries and the Recent Projects section. Tighten around consulting impact, senior advisory value, and 2–3 concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet about improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Replace feature lists with outcomes where possible: size of web properties, number of teams supported, launch status, efficiency gains, engagement lift, reduced publishing time, or improved content findability.
- Use stronger consulting verbs: “advised,” “designed,” “implemented,” “launched,” “streamlined,” “defined,” rather than “build and refine” or “deliver.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” overlaps with Director of Digital Media; frame this as post-tenure advisory/optimization work.
- Microsites and AI search are already covered in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s newsletter/video execution details.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s enterprise digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Recast bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more strategic and measurable: add growth, engagement, deliverability, production volume, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten this bullet.
- Tighten operations bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio…” and “Expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve leadership reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current email/newsletter and recurring video language overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and systems.
- “Governance/publishing standards/workflows” also appears in multiple NACo roles; use distinct wording here tied to org-wide scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong mid-career progression item, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo role above and the earlier digital media role below. Tighten it around execution, team coordination, and channel growth outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Combine newsletter and audience impact: “Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Sharpen operations language: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency across digital channels.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap; merge into one stronger operations bullet.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight language already used in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing enterprise leadership and governance rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, less overlapping bullets such as:
- Enterprise digital strategy and operating models
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content workflows
- Cross-channel communications leadership for complex organizations
- Public-sector stakeholder engagement and advocacy storytelling
- Audience-centered content planning and information design
- Use noun phrases with parallel structure; avoid broad terms like “messaging” unless tied to audience or organizational context.
- If space allows elsewhere, move proof points like “10,000+ page migration” or “50+ internal publishers” into experience bullets rather than skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)
- Platform integrations and workflow automation
- SharePoint, Power Pages and Airtable-based business systems
- AI-enabled search and content discovery
- Drop lower-signal or dated phrasing like “jQuery” unless it is directly relevant to target roles.
- Group tools under broader capabilities to keep this section concise and executive-level.
- If possible, align wording to recent impact: “enterprise CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search” are stronger than listing platforms alone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlap with Core Competencies; keep only the sharper phrasing here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This Topline Skills item should emphasize strategic analytics leadership, not repeat the software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools here; move the full stack to Technical + IT.
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI and Looker Studio • User behavior and performance analysis”
- If accurate, strengthen with scope language tied to recent work: “enterprise analytics,” “cross-channel reporting,” or “decision-ready dashboards.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the Technical + IT item almost exactly; avoid listing the same tools in both places.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader digital strategy unless you can show it as a distinct strength.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Make it tighter, more senior, and oriented to delivery capability rather than listing basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize leadership-level execution: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more distinctive phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to sound less entry-level.
- Consider swapping “Hybrid and virtual event production” for “Hybrid event production and technical delivery” to stress operational ownership.
- If space allows, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work: “in-house studio buildout” or “advocacy programming production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”); use more specific wording here.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent platform in the experience section, give it prominence and consider trimming lower-signal items.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider emphasizing depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If formatting allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If you want more concision, rename the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** and keep the list tight.
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if space is tight; it reads less strategic than the other platforms given your senior leadership profile.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution** entry almost exactly.
- Avoid repeating platform names elsewhere unless this section adds specificity (e.g., Drupal scale or migration context).

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior recent-profile CV, this item should emphasize implementation tools that support delivery, automation, and modern web operations.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a tighter, more senior-oriented list: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group operational tools separately: “Technical operations: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope or level in parentheses to signal depth, e.g., “JavaScript (custom UI behavior), GTM (tag deployment), GitHub Actions (deployment automation)”
- Consider dropping version numbers unless required; “HTML” and “CSS” are cleaner than “HTML5” and “CSS3”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills
- GTM may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless you want this section strictly implementation-focused

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so it should be tighter and more purposeful.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Project/issue management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Team collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “used to support cross-team publishing, approvals, and communications operations.”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clarity and specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating them prominently in multiple sections.
- Slack and Teams are low-signal unless central to operations leadership; they can be cut if space is tight.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. It would be stronger if it signaled level of use and aligned to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations without repeating work-experience bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Rename for precision: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these are all current/credible hands-on tools; otherwise remove any weaker/older platform.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member email/community communications) • Mailchimp (newsletter operations)**
- Put the most recent/strategic platform first; if Dynamics 365 is the newest enterprise tool, keep it first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work-experience references to email newsletters; avoid adding outcomes here unless they are not already stated elsewhere.
- “Engagement” may feel vague since social/community tools are not listed; “Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms” is clearer.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the stronger “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and recent NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize technical platforms and remove broad capability terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • Google Optimize/experiment platforms**
- Replace broad terms like **SEO**, **A/B testing**, and **Dashboarding** with specific tools or methods; if no tool names are available, use **SEO analysis** and **experiment design**.
- Order by strongest/recently used platforms first: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity**.
- If space allows, add one differentiator tied to impact elsewhere in the CV, e.g. **KPI reporting** or **analytics infrastructure**, but only if not repeated nearby.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one of the two.
- “SEO,” “A/B testing,” and “Dashboarding” are capability labels already implied by the experience bullets.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to foundational team-building and content production.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream/event volume, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence around contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised a digital media associate’s day-to-day work.”
- If true, name tools/platforms or process wins that show early leadership: editorial calendar, publishing standards, video workflow, cross-team coordination.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or piloting the format.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” risks repeating later governance/operations bullets; keep this entry focused on foundational build-out.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize cross-functional coordination and the podcast launch as the clearest outcome.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest accomplishment: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific line such as: “Produced digital and multimedia content to translate research and policy work into member-facing communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Keep this entry to 1–2 lines since later roles already show broader digital leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic multimedia language already covered in later NACo roles (video, digital content, production).
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; save team-building/platform impact for 2015–present roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed capability list than a tight tools section. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills, so keep this entry software/tool-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production systems • Podcast recording/editing**
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with “Livestream production systems” or specific tools/platforms if available; “workflows” is vague for a technical skills list.
- Tighten “Podcast production” to “Podcast recording/editing” unless you want to emphasize strategy elsewhere.
- If accurate, add one higher-value recent tool or platform used in current/recent roles (for example, OBS, vMix, StreamYard, Riverside, or Adobe Creative Cloud) to make the list more concrete.
